meta.title: feat: migrate tests from Bun to Vitest with parallel execution
meta.body_summary: Migrate Alchemy tests from Bun to Vitest with parallel thread-pool execution, updating 50+ test imports, adding vitest config, and maintaining backward compatibility via test runner flags.

perf_labels.notes: Devin migrated 50+ test files to Vitest; maintainer gave feedback on script naming and prune logic, which were addressed, but PR was later closed without merge, possibly due to maintainer decision against automated test framework migration.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 548 changed lines across 57 files, this is a medium-sized change by absolute volume, mostly import updates and a vitest helper. As a test infrastructure migration, it was closed without merging after maintainer feedback was addressed.

review_details.concern_detail: Maintainer sam-goodwin requested using prune logic for vitest, removing separate test:vitest in favor of replacing 'test' script with vitest via prune, and adding a test:force script to bypass prune.
review_details.performance_claim: Parallel Vitest execution will reduce test suite runtime.
review_details.antipattern_addressed: sequential_test_execution (prior behavior; not in taxonomy enum)
review_details.rejection_signals: Maintainer closed PR without merging after feedback was addressed; no explicit rejection reason provided. Possibly maintainer decided not to adopt the automated migration.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Test framework migration across 50+ files and build config is technically feasible for the agent, but the merge decision rests with the maintainer's willingness to accept AI-generated test infra changes, which may be influenced by trust or strategic preference.

detection_detail.code_reading: Maintainer reviewed package.json script changes and requested tweaks via inline comments.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: PR claims faster test execution via parallelization but provides no before/after timing data; reproducibility of the performance claim is impossible without benchmarks.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: Devin added commits to integrate prune logic, rename script, and add test:force per maintainer feedback, but PR was later closed without merge.

core_change_summary.description: Migrated all test imports from bun:test to vitest, added vitest.config.ts with parallel thread pool, created vitest test helper replicating bun test helper, updated prune logic to support vitest, and adjusted matchers for compatibility.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: The remaining 50+ test files had only import path changes (bun:test → vitest) with minimal other edits.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: full migration, vitest helper, config, script updates.
Fix: use prune logic for vitest test script.
Replace test script to use vitest by default and remove test:vitest.
Add test:force script to skip prune logic.

review_signals.summary: I'd still like to use the prune logic if we can when using vitest
review_signals.action_taken: Devin updated test:vitest to use runner with --vitest flag in subsequent commit.

review_signals.summary: i think we can just replace test, we don't need a test:vitest because the test codes explicitly use vitest now
review_signals.action_taken: Devin replaced the test script to use vitest by default and removed test:vitest.

review_signals.summary: let's add test:force that skips the prune logic
review_signals.action_taken: Devin added test:force script using bun vitest run directly.

review_signals.summary: Devin bot announced automatic comment/CI assistance for write-access users.
pkg-pr-new posted a StackBlitz preview link for the PR build.

collaboration_trajectory: Devin opened PR with full vitest migration.
Within minutes, maintainer sam-goodwin left three inline comments on package.json requesting prune integration, script consolidation, and a force-run option.
Devin responded with three follow-up commits addressing each comment (use prune, remove test:vitest, add test:force).
PR was closed by maintainer after ~5.5 hours, without merge, despite all feedback addressed.
